children: India’s BSE Sensex traded nearly flat on Thursday, to around 74,732, halting a recent decline after falling to its lowest level in nearly three months.

The market remained under pressure from escalating Middle East tensions, with Brent crude holding above $100 a barrel, raising concerns over India’s import bill, inflation, economic growth and corporate margins.
The rupee weakened to around 95.10 per U.S. dollar on Wednesday despite intervention by the Reserve Bank of India.
Energy stocks provided some support, with ONGC (+2.0%) and Oil India (+2.4%) advancing as higher crude prices boosted the outlook for upstream producers.
Shakti Pumps (+10.4%) also jumped after securing a ?235.92 crore order to supply 10,000 solar pumps, while Axis Bank, Bajaj Finserv and Larsen & Toubro were among the early Sensex gainers.
Investors remained cautious ahead of US inflation data and the Federal Reserve’s September policy meeting.

title: Sensex Halts Decline Amid Oil, Geopolitical Risks
